Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis: Patient has a history of chronic warfarin-refractory deep vein thromboses and placement of a nonretrievable inferior vena cava filter, indicating a hypercoagulable state. Transthoracic echocardiography showed a 1.6 x 0.9 cm tricuspid-valve vegetation, and transesophageal echocardiography confirmed vegetations on all three tricuspid leaflets, consistent with nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis.
Systemic lupus erythematosus: Patient has a malar rash, symmetric wrist stiffness, and laboratory results showing elevated ESR and CRP, which are consistent with systemic lupus erythematosus. The patient's history of heavy menstrual bleeding, miscarriage, and chronic deep vein thromboses also suggests a possible autoimmune disorder.
